# improve-generating phase 2: joint report (`gen-v4` in production)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Authors | SA-Opus (drafter, round 1), SA-Astra (reviewer); one agreed text |
| Base | `gen-v4` at `7c1bad2`; draft PR #14 into `main`, not merged |
| Sources | both round-1 analyses and cross-reviews, `evidence/sa-astra/round1-cross-audit.*`, `evidence/sa-opus/p2-*` |
| Plan, questions | [plan.md](plan.md) (Draft, round 1), [clarifications.md](clarifications.md) |

## Summary

- **What phase 2 does.** It puts the frozen `gen-v4` search into the production code for Nightmare and Hell 1, with
  the class choices of the frozen round:
  - the 190 M screen only on Nightmare boards of 196 to 256 cells;
  - the prior table;
  - the per-set prior on Hell 1;
  - the call budgets and the bound of four set attempts.

  Today's search stays on the full 26x26 Nightmare board and on every level up to Master.
- **Identity and replay.** Every new record carries `gen-v4` with seven version keys. Old records stay playable, and
  their generation steps are refused by version.
- **Deadline.** The Generator's two actions keep 115/120 s each. Automatic `gen-v4` requests of the CLI and the bench
  share one 46/115/120-s clock. A real hard guard bounds the response, pack assembly included.
- **Validation before anything ships.**
  - proof bundles and smoke requests;
  - equality with the frozen arms on every measured row;
  - the (c5) re-check of the one screened class;
  - conditional P5 comparisons;
  - `require` on the largest boards first;
  - 140 rows on boards without a prior cell.
- **Price: 812 counted minutes**, stage A (410) and then, after a readout, stage B (402). It is a spend cap, not a
  promise of completion.
- **Effort:** about 46 developer hours in 17 tasks.
- **Owner questions:** Q-P2-1 (the 812 minutes and how they are funded) and Q-P2-5 (the English and Vietnamese texts).
  All other questions were settled by the two SAs under the owner's delegation.

## 1. What the owner asked

- **D-S24-35** (Q-T16 (a), 2026-11-25): today's search is kept on 26x26 Nightmare, and `gen-v4` is proposed for the
  other boards with the recorded class choices. The phase-2 pack must:
  - implement the route;
  - prove compatibility and replay;
  - measure `require` on the largest boards first (N-V4-15);
  - repeat the validation on the production code;
  - come back with its plan and price before anything runs or ships.

  The phase-0 FAIL stays recorded and Hell 1's offer rules are unchanged (`request.md:35-40`; register `ca46067`).
- **Branch and PR.** Phase 2 lives on `gen-v4`, from the published phase-1 head, with a PR into `main`. Neither PR is
  merged (`c63c553`, `request.md:21-27`).
- **Delegation.** The two SAs answer supervisor-level questions jointly (`request.md:29-31`).

## 2. What the two analyses established

| Finding | Evidence |
|---|---|
| The frozen implementation cannot be copied: journals, `IG` globals and Node imports, built on `3fc65f4` before phase 1 | `evidence/sa-opus/p2-variant-chain.md`; `ig-select-v4.js:23-30, 226` |
| Only `n-mid` ships the screen, so the production screen table needs its own id; the frozen selector's classes are wider | `freeze.json` `values.W`; `stage4-report.md:36-55`; `ig-select-v4.js:97-132` |
| The Generator page offers boards up to 484 cells (360 on a phone) and no Hell 1. The CLI defaults to 676 cells, so the 26x26 route does reach users | `policy.js:24-31`; `state.js:322-324`; `tools/generate.mjs:40` |
| The CLI and the bench make a set and a batch in one request; the Generator's two actions are separate requests | `generate.mjs:548-562`; `generator/jobs.js:303-440` |
| The 120-s response bound is defined but enforced nowhere today; `finish(job)` precedes pack assembly; the Generator's job times use `Date.now`, the pool `performance.now` | `policy.js:69`; `generation-client.js:1172-1186`; `jobs.js:201`; `worker-pool.js:132-136` |
| The frozen live deadline acted only with a host origin, which only the bench gave | `live.json` `lv-9`..`lv-12`; `lane-worker.mjs:186` |
| The longest `gen-v4` Nightmare set stage on an offered board was 16.1 s; the 46-s reserve cut acted once, on 14x14 Hell 1 rep 33 | `evidence/sa-opus/p2-xr-setstage.md` |

## 3. How the two analyses were reconciled

| Point | SA-Opus, round 1 | SA-Astra, round 1 | Agreed |
|---|---|---|---|
| 26x26 route | every Nightmare board above 576 cells | the exact full 26x26 board | the exact board: 26 by 26, 676 active cells, rotation-independent (D-S24-35's words) |
| Deadline | no shared clock at all | the 46-s cut also on a standalone set | Generator actions 115/120 s each; one 46/115/120-s clock for automatic `gen-v4` CLI and bench requests; a real host guard |
| Seeds | frozen reps 20-39 | fresh reps 60-79 | reps 20-39 (Master 20-24) as a source-port replication with no retuning; 40-59 reserved |
| Port proof | equality on every row | reference parity in tests | four proof bundles and eight smoke requests, then equality on every eligible row before any ratio is read |
| (c5) | not repeated | repeated for `n-mid` | repeated: the fixed three-cell panel |
| P5 comparison | none (carried by equality) | 360 unconditional twins | twins for every row that meets a predeclared trigger; analytical zeros reported apart; 15 priced slots, not a quota |
| `require` (N-V4-15) | Nightmare, today and `gen-v4` | Nightmare and Hell 1, bounded and uncapped | 50 rows: Nightmare with three arms, Hell 1 diagnostic with two |
| Boards without a prior cell | 80 rows | not measured | 140 sentinel rows, 20 per arm, gates declared before the run |
| Counters | in the production result | a trace in measurement copies | both: minimal counts in production, the detailed trace in symmetric copies |
| Price | 377 expected, 480 envelope | 945, or 1,126 for full breadth | 812, enumerated by SA-Astra and reproduced row by row by SA-Opus (`p2-xr-verify-astra.md`) |
| Screen table | `screen-p2-v1` | `screen-v4-v1` | `screen-v4-v1` |
| No-window texts | "every clue count tried" | "without finding a suitable window" | plain words that state only what the search did; the technical wording is the owner's alternative |

## 4. The agreed design in brief

The plan has the details (sections 4 and 5).

- **Route.** `gen-v4` for Hell 1 and for Nightmare except the exact 26x26 board; every other level runs `gen-v3`'s
  selection. The route governs every stage.
- **Identity.**
  - Algo `gen-v4` for all new records, with the seven keys and the tables `prior-s3-v1` and `screen-v4-v1`.
  - The budgets, the bound, the re-rating rule, the deadline and the route belong to the `gen-v4` definition; no
    eighth key.
  - `made.igPrior` and subset ordinals below 2,192.
- **Search.** The frozen P1 to P5 with P6 kept. Prior by exact key, otherwise `K - 8` with step 8. The per-set prior
  on Hell 1 only. Budgets: `any` 10 G (Nightmare) and 40 G (Hell 1); `require` 32 G and 40 G.
- **Deadline.** As in the summary. The set loop keeps the frozen order. At the hard bound the host returns the consumed
  fold prefix and fences late results.
- **Replay.** `replay-case.json` stays the `gen-v3` refusal case. There are new `gen-v4` cases, and the 10x6 fixtures
  change in their versions only. The saved-steps key holds the running tuple, and `REPLAY` is re-derived.
- **Texts.** The new step sentences and notices are in English and Vietnamese. Both SAs recommend a plain-language
  wording for the four no-window strings; an equally accurate technical alternative is offered to the owner. The "no
  fail-fast" statement of `design-detail.md:1805` is replaced (plan 4.11).

## 5. The production validation and its price

The matrix:
- the 19 frozen Nightmare and Hell 1 cells on the shipped code;
- today's search on the ten controls;
- 16 Master cells on both arms;
- `n-mid` without the screen;
- 140 sentinel rows;
- 50 `require` rows;
- eight smoke rows;
- up to 15 planned conditional twins.

That is 1,013 rows, plus four proof bundles, eight resource replays and six browser checks.

**Pricing basis.**
- Each row is priced at its matching frozen mean response + 2 s. The frozen row steps really took 0.99 to 1.08 s beyond
  their responses, and no P6 credit is taken.
- `require` and unknown twins are priced at their row limits.
- The proof bundles are priced at their measured cost.
- The schedule follows the 885/900/45-s rules.

| Stage | Rows | Counted min | Guard min | Authorization |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| A: proofs, smoke, `require`, sentinels, thin controls, replays, browser checks | 318 | 330.656 | 409.195 | 410 |
| B: the rest of the matrix and the conditional twins | 695 | 321.258 | 401.572 | 402 |
| Total | 1,013 | 651.913 | 810.767 | **812** |

- **Spend cap.** The sentinels' times are weak neighbour proxies; at their row limits the cap would be 1,303 minutes.
  812 is therefore a spend cap: observations beyond it stop incomplete, never counted as passes.
- **Funding.** The closed round's grant has 853.8 of 1,725 minutes left. We recommend a separate phase-2 ledger; the
  owner may instead expressly authorize 812 from that balance. Nothing rolls over by default.

## 6. Questions for the owner

| Q-P2-1 | Approve the validation and 812 counted minutes (410, then 402 after the stage-A readout), and say which account pays | approve, with a separate phase-2 ledger |

Both are in [clarifications.md](clarifications.md). Until Q-P2-1 is answered, no measurement runs (P2-18 to P2-20).
Until Q-P2-5 is answered, the text task (P2-09) waits. The developer tasks before them can start once the plan is final.

## 7. What follows

- The validation report, then PR #14's description (no merge).

**Interfaces.**

### 4.2 The route

- Every other level, Very easy to Master and Hell 2 and above, runs `gen-v3`'s selection unchanged.
- The route governs the set calibration, the batch candidates, the completion pass, P5, the prior, the deadline scope

- Reach today: the Generator page offers Nightmare on 81 to 484 cells (360 on a phone) and no Hell 1. The CLI reaches

- **Seven keys** (IG-P-Q36): `algo`, `policy`, `rng`, `seedScheme`, `ratingModel`, `priorTable`, `screenTable`. Other

### 4.4 The search (port contract)

For the same effective request, production `gen-v4` returns the frozen shipped arm's puzzle keys, work units and skip
ordinals. P6 changes no key; a clock stop changes only how many puzzles a response holds.

| Part | Contract |
|---|---|
| P1 | the locate of plan P1 (`plan.md:161-239`): nested family, march from the start count, bisection, window choice, the AR1 direction (a refused profile keeps its canonical score for direction, never for acceptance or the stall count) |
| P2 | screen ratings at `W`; certified when the main-phase work (`work - censusWork`) is at most `W`, then equal to the canonical rating; otherwise screen-capped: direction only, never accepted, never shown as a score; the rescue re-rates screen-capped locate probes, sharing the allowance of four with the tail re-rating |
| P3 | a capped profile is `TOO_FEW`, a direction; `tests/clues.test.js:820` keeps pinning `gen-v3`, and `gen-v4` gets its own test |
| P4 | exact key `<level>@<active cells>` in `prior-s3-v1`: start `clamp(round(share x K), 1, K - 2)` with step 1; without a cell, start `K - 8` with step 8 (no interpolation, no refit). The per-set prior applies to Hell 1 only, from a matching calibration (same set and layout, level and uniqueness; a unique certificate for `require`), else the table; the completion pass takes no per-set override; calibration stays session-only |
| P5 budget | per call: `any` 10,000,000,000 units (Nightmare), 40,000,000,000 (Hell 1); `require` 32,000,000,000 and 40,000,000,000. Checked before each primitive, so the last primitive can overshoot; the uniqueness repair's `onAdd` check is always installed; at the stop `any` may return a waiting in-band result, `require` only a finished unique final; no rating or count starts after it |
| P5 bound | the request's set stage ends `no-window-below` or `no-window-above` when attempts 0 to 3 all ended without a window on the same side. A budget stop has no side. The bound is read before the ordered winner scan, so a later success cannot override it |

### 4.5 The deadline

- **Generator actions.** "New piece set" and "New puzzle" each get a fresh monotonic scope from the pool's clock: a
  115-s generation stop and a 120-s hard response bound, no reserve. No clock spans the user's pause, and no `Date.now`
  reading reaches the pool.
- **Automatic requests.** A `gen-v4`-route CLI request and a bench row make the set and the batch under one scope with
  `deadline-s3-v1`:
  - the set stage is cut at 46 s (reserve 0.6);
  - generation stops at 115 s;
  - the response is bounded at 120 s, the host acting at 119 s (1-s margin).
- **Legacy routes** (Master and below, the 26x26 exception) keep their two timers.
- **The set loop order:** cancellation or time-out, the same-side bound, the ordered winner scan, the reserve cut, a new
  dispatch.
- **Host guard.** `generation-deadline.js` covers the whole response, pack assembly included. At the work stop it
  cancels outstanding tasks. At the hard bound it returns the consumed, validated fold prefix with its `made` records
  and seen histories, without awaiting a held assembly. It fences late completions by request id and revision and
  gives one terminal result. A shown puzzle stays in the history (phase 1's policy).

### 4.6 Counters and traces

- **The production selection result** carries integer counts: budget stops, set attempts ended `no-window-*` and bound
  firings, screen-capped profiles, rescue and tail re-ratings. They pass through the worker result to the client and
  the bench rows. They are never part of an identity and need no `record` or `onRate`, so P6 stays on.
- **The validation** takes primitive starts, ends and cancellations from an identified trace in the measurement copies
  of both arms. It is proved not to change puzzles, work or skips; no claim of zero overhead is made. The counters
  alone cannot bound work abandoned by a cancellation.
- **Browser deadline checks** run on the shipping build.

### 4.7 Records, replay and fixtures

- `tests/fixtures/replay-case.json` stays byte for byte: it loads, keeps its provenance through a load and a save, and
  replays "unavailable" with `set-versions`.
- A new `gen-v4` replay fixture re-records the Hard recipe; the five readers (`replay`, `replay-model`, `protocol`,
  `tasks`, `generation-client` tests) move to it. A second `gen-v4` case covers the screen path on a Nightmare board of
  196 to 256 cells (at least one locate and one screen-capped event), found by a bounded seed search. It is marked slow
  where needed, within the 10-minute suite limit.
- The large 26x26 legacy-route replay runs in the legacy-route proof bundle under the lock, not in `npm test`.
- `generation-case.json` and `generated-sample-pack.json` are re-recorded with `record-fixtures.mjs --replace --reason`.
  Only the versions change; the semantic keys and scores must not (a scope proof). `record-fixtures.mjs` checks the
  refusal case apart from regenerating the matched cases.
- New events (phases `locate`, `window`, `rescue`; reason `screen-capped`; budget and no-window ends) map to steps. A
  screen-capped step shows no score.
- The saved-steps key includes the running seven-key tuple, or the tuple is checked before a cached result is shown.
- `REPLAY` (steps, bytes, work) is re-derived from measured `gen-v4` replays, the budget overshoot included. A bound is
  not raised to make an incomplete replay pass.

### 4.8 Migration and compatibility

- **No data migration.** `gen-v3` sets, packs and histories load and play unchanged. Their Generation steps are
  unavailable with today's reasons, and so are the steps of a new puzzle made on a set saved before the release
  (`plan.md:792-795`).
- **Nothing is restamped;** old records keep their five keys through a load and a save.
- **Forward compatibility.** An older build reading a `gen-v4` pack drops the `made` record it cannot read, with a
  warning, and keeps the puzzles. One check with the `6b94ffb` reader confirms it.
- **The pack and puzzle-code formats, the app version, the policy, the RNG and the seed scheme do not change.**

### 7.5 The conditional P5 comparator and its report

- **Eligible rows:** the 360 shipped `gen-v4` rows (the legacy 26x26 excluded) and the 80 `gen-v4` sentinel rows. The

- **Trigger, fixed before the run.** The production row or its frozen counterpart shows any of:
  - fewer than ten puzzles;
  - a set attempt ended `no-window-*`, or the bound fired;
  - a call budget stop;
  - a reserve cut, the work stop or the host bound.

  A missing outcome or reach field is unknown, never zero.
- **The twin:** the same request on the uncapped copy.
- **Readings:** a false stop is a bound firing whose twin makes a set; a lost completion is a bounded row below ten
  whose twin reaches ten (`tools/ig-proto/verdicts.mjs:1366-1441`).

- **The report's columns:** eligible rows, analytical zeros, observed pairs, false stops, lost completions, and required
  twins still missing. The coverage categories are disjoint:
  - analytical-only: both endpoints settled, no measured twin;
  - observed pair: any row with a measured twin, even if its zero was deducible;
  - unresolved: a required twin is missing.
